Claim.description:
One source's statement about one field. Frozen and scalar (tuples for lists), so claims are
hashable and set-comparable. `fetched_at` comes from the cache entry, never from build time.
Claim.title: Claim

Dedup.description:
Corpus-wide ingest merges from the snapshot manifest (PRISMA-S item 16): a process statement, never a
removal count of this search. The not-merged counts are the manifest's conflicts by resolution: pairs
that looked alike but were kept apart (two candidates from one source; a track the proceedings never
host; two records of one venue-year). The last two are None on a v1 body, which didn't record them.
Dedup.title: Dedup

Diagnostic.description: A warning, error or translation notice about a query, with a half-open code-point span into `q`.
Diagnostic.title: Diagnostic

Excluded.description:
What the default filters removed (spec 03 §Exclusion accounting): the buckets sum to `total`, each
map is ordered by count (largest first, ties by name) with `unknown` last and always present.
Excluded.title: Excluded

Facets.description:
Disjunctive (decision-001): each field counted without its own top-level conjuncts. Values that
occur only; years as strings.
Facets.title: Facets

Filter.description:
`field:` restricted to any of `values` (a single-field OR group): YearRanges for `year`, canonical
strings (`vocab.py`) for the others.
Filter.title: Filter

index_versions.description: every index on this instance, sorted; the served one included
index_versions.title: Index Versions

Near.description: Both operands within `distance` words of each other, in either order, in one field.
Near.title: Near

ParseResponse.description:
02's `ParseResult` without `identification_ast` (it stays server-side; spec 04 §Endpoints). A query
with errors is still a 200 here: `errors` holds them, and every Optional is null.
ParseResponse.title: ParseResponse

Phrase.description: Consecutive positions in one field. A wildcard item is expanded at its position (decision-001).
Phrase.title: Phrase

RecordExcluded.description: 03's exclusion accounting, verbatim: buckets by count (largest first, ties by name), `unknown` last.
RecordExcluded.title: RecordExcluded

SearchRecord.description:
Every field of spec 04 §Search records, plus `body_version`, `schema_version` and `ranking_params`
(the index's other two inputs, so a drifted replay can name a method change after the pinned index is
gone). `ids` is None when the caller didn't ask for them.

Body version 2 adds `sources` (the snapshot manifest's source names, sorted), `identification_citable`
(false when every source is a bootstrap one, `vocab.bootstrap_only`: the corpus is an earlier search's
output, so `total` is not a PRISMA identification number) and `crawl_dates_kind` (per `crawl_dates` key:
`crawl`, `scholar_query_dates` or `mixed`), and `dedup`'s two other not-merged counts. A v1 body has
none of them: they read as None ("not recorded"), never as a guess.
SearchRecord.title: SearchRecord

SnapshotInfo.description: The snapshot the served index was built from, as its manifest records it.
SnapshotInfo.title: SnapshotInfo

StoredDiagnostic.description: A diagnostic as the record saved it: its code is a string, so a retired code stays readable.
StoredDiagnostic.title: StoredDiagnostic

VenueYearCoverage.description:
One venue-year of the snapshot (`coverage.breakdown`): its cells in vocabulary order (`unknown`
last, never folded), and its unknown and missing-abstract counts, 0 included.
VenueYearCoverage.title: VenueYearCoverage

Wildcard.description: A suffix wildcard on one normalised token: `*` is zero or more characters, `$` zero or one.
Wildcard.title: Wildcard

get.description: The served index's coverage, computed and checked when it was loaded.

Every record the query matches, in `format`: of `q` (with `mode`, default `native`) on the pinned
`index_version` (else the served index), or the stored ids of search record `record_id` (alone) from the
index it names. Never paginated or truncated; `X-Total` equals `/search`'s `total` for the same query and
index (for a record, its stored `total`).

200.description: The entire matched set, ordered by id, with `X-Total`, `X-Index-Version`, `X-Tokenizer-Version` and `X-Query-Version`.

get.description:
Always 200 while the process serves requests; `index_loaded` is false until the first load succeeds
(search routes answer 503 `API_INDEX_NOT_LOADED` meanwhile).
The paper with this id in the served index, as its snapshot holds it.

post.description:
02's ParseResult for `q` (debounced as the user types). It reports a parse: any well-formed body is
a 200 whose `errors` say why the query doesn't parse (`PARSE_TOO_LONG` included); only a malformed body
is refused (422 `API_BAD_PARAM`).
Freeze a search as an immutable record: re-run here on the served index, then one transaction.

get.description:
The stored record and a replay of it now (HTTP 200 whatever the status). `ids` is null unless
`include=ids`; `/export?record_id=` streams the papers themselves.

The ids a replay now adds and removes, with titles, and which `index_version` inputs changed. Each
list is paged by `offset`/`limit` (≤ 200, never clamped); `added_total`/`removed_total` are in full. A
title comes from the index the replay ran on, null if it doesn't hold the paper. A refused replay
compared nothing: empty lists, null totals.

One page of the ranked matched set, with its total, exclusion accounting, disjunctive facets and
highlights. `limit` over 200 is a 422 (never clamped); a query that doesn't parse is a 422 with its
diagnostics.
